# Homework 2

## 2.1
Consider the following list of ARSs

1. $\quad A=\{\}$.
2. $\quad A=\{a\}\quad$ and $\quad {R}=\{\}$.
3. $\quad A=\{a\}\quad$ and $\quad {R}=\{(a,a)\}$.
4. $\quad A=\{a,b,c\}\quad$ and $\quad {R}=\{(a,b),(a,c)\}$.
5. $\quad A=\{a,b\}\quad$ and $\quad {R}=\{(a,a),(a,b)\}$.
6. $\quad A=\{a,b,c\}\quad$ and $\quad {R}=\{(a,b),(b,b),(a,c)\}$.
7. $\quad A=\{a,b,c\}\quad$ and $\quad {R}=\{(a,b),(b,b),(a,c),(c,c)\}$.

Draw a picture for each of the ARSs above.[^directedGraph]
    
[^directedGraph]: If you wonder how to draw a picture of an ARS, remember that an ARS is nothing but a [directed graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_graph).

Are the ARSs terminating? Are they confluent? Do they have unique normal forms? 


## 2.2
Try to find an example of an ARS for each of the possible 8 combinations. Draw pictures of these examples.

| confluent | terminating | has unique normal forms | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| True | True | True | 
| True | True | False | 
| True | False | True | 
| True | False | False | 
| False | True | True | 
| False | True | False | 
| False | False | True | 
| False | False | False |
